state.rules: A readiness rule set evaluates independently owned mutable subjects. A complete assessment means all required rule-subject results are present, with unknowns and gaps disclosed. An Org Admin may enter Type I using an exact completed historical assessment, including one with gaps; the decision lists the gaps with their plans. Gaps and plans are separately owned. The meaning of a missing plan is undecided.
state.proposal: Each rule-subject-result is independently recorded. A paged read service derives the aggregate verdict and lists gaps. A decision owner stores a reference to one assessment and rationale. No aggregate owns a child list, and no write decision may require inspecting or waiting for every child. A materialized result is eventually consistent unless a validated immutable source cut proves the required set and every result. Neither zero projection rows nor counts guarantee source completeness.

projected_zero.instructions: Can a lagging projection containing zero gaps prove that an assessment with required but not yet projected subjects has no gaps?

read_rollup.instructions: Can a read service show a calculated rollup and stream individual results without placing those individual results into a parent aggregate?

gate_still_global.instructions: If a write is refused until the status of every individual result is complete, does the write decision still depend on all those results even when another service computed the status?

weakened_guard.instructions: Does allowing a management decision when the cited assessment is incomplete weaken the stated requirement to use a complete assessment?

previous_snapshot.instructions: Under the stated policy, can an exactly reproducible complete historical assessment remain eligible even after newer source facts exist?

latest_plan.instructions: Does showing a gap plan as it exists today necessarily show the plan as it existed at the time of a decision made last week?

pending_unknown.instructions: If required subjects may be missing from the projection, is it justified to mark assessment completeness as unknown rather than complete?

key_collision.instructions: If one rule can emit two distinct gaps for one subject, can keying both gap plans only by the rule and subject cause the two gaps to share a plan identity?

cut_claim.instructions: Does citing an assessment identifier alone prove an immutable complete snapshot exists with all required evidence?

unknown_verdict.instructions: Given a policy that any unknown required input yields incomplete, can an assessment with one known gap and one unknown required input be called not_ready instead of incomplete under that policy?
